text:
Maria: quick heads-up — spun a 5% canary of v5.2-quant4 (longdoc optimizer) this morning. shadow vs v5.1-fp16 shows ~12.3% drop in rerank MRR on long-doc slice and p95 latency +30ms. rolling at 5% now. not sure if kv-prefix mismatch or quant noise. anyone seen this pattern before? :eyes:

Kai: put the raw diff here from shadow run — looks like the regression is concentrated on >2k token prompts and when KV warmup count is low:
```
slice: longdoc_top10
metric: rerank_mrr
v5.1-fp16: 0.421
v5.2-quant4: 0.369
delta: -0.052 (-12.3%)
latency.p95: 180ms -> 210ms
```
Not typical hallucination spike, more scoring/rerank mismatch. also saw slightly higher token variance during kv-restore.

Devin: ugh. canary config currently has autofallback thresholds at {mrr_drop: 7%, halluc_rate_abs: 2%}. For longdoc slices we should be stricter. propose immediate abort/fallback if mrr_drop > 5% OR p95_latency_increase > 20ms OR kv_warmup_miss_rate > 1%. That would have tripped here.

Maria: SG. I'll patch the promote policy. suggested patch snippet to the rollout config:
```yaml
canary: 5%
auto_fallback:
  - metric: rerank_mrr
    threshold_pct: 5.0
    window_secs: 600
  - metric: latency_p95_ms
    threshold_abs: 20
    window_secs: 600
  - metric: kv_warmup_miss_rate_pct
    threshold_pct: 1.0
    window_secs: 600
```
Applying now and will reduce canary to 1% until we have warmer KV traces.

Kai: also push a short-term mitigation: force route-level kv_warmup=10 for the canary pool so caches populate before scoring. That should reduce the cold-kv noise without changing model config. I'll open a CL. :mechanical_arm:

oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-2043 — "v5.2-quant4 longdoc mrr regression (canary)". Automatic watcher attached: eng-ml, eng-platform.

Maria: thanks — monitoring dashboards updated. if autofallback triggers we let it rollback automatically; otherwise we'll keep canary at 1% and run an expanded shadow with kv_warmup=10 to verify. tagging @dev-sre for infra warmup assistance. :thumbsup:
